newsitem.title: USA: Dillon Read seen one of best-managed U.S. brokers.
newsitem.headline: Dillon Read seen one of best-managed U.S. brokers.

text.p: Dillon, Read & Co Inc, one of the best-managed U.S. investment banks, was seen as a timely and prize catch for Swiss Bank Corp as Wall Street goes through a wave of consolidation.
Analysts noted Dillon Read has concentrated on highly profitable advisory work and avoided some of the volatile Wall Street areas such as fixed income trading.

They said Swiss Bank, which is buying Dillon Read for about $600 million stock and combining it with its SBC Warburg investment bank, will probably give Dillon Read free rein to do what it has done in the past.

"Dillon Read is a very conservatively managed company that does not try to be all things to all people," said Perrin Long, an independent analyst. "They have a strong and highly profitable advisory business."
Long said the deal was "a real coup" for Swiss Bank. "They got a great name."
"Dillon Read clearly has a quality client franchise," Simon Canning, chief executive and president of the section 20 subsidiary of Swiss Bank Corp in New York, said in a telephone interview.
Canning said the acquisition will create "the most international of the global investment banking firms in our spread of clients worldwide."

In 1996, Dillon Read was an adviser on 50 mergers and acquisitions deals with an aggregate value of $45 billion. Dillon Read's deals in high yield, equity offerings and private placements totaled $8 billion last year.
The acquisition of Dillon Read by Swiss Bank comes at a time when U.S. financial service firms are being caught up in a wave of consolidation.

The two most talked-about deals this year are the still pending mergers of investment banking powerhouse Morgan Stanley group Inc with Dean Witter Discover & Co and Bankers Trust New York Corp with Alex. Brown Inc.

Following announcement of those two deals, speculation about other possible mergers reached a fever pitch with privately-held Oppenheimer & Co and Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc among the rumored targets.
